newsitem.title: USA: Food Lion jurors weighed damages of up to $1.7 bln.
newsitem.headline: Food Lion jurors weighed damages of up to $1.7 bln.

text.p: Jurors who ordered Walt Disney Co 's ABC-TV unit to pay $5.5 million in punitive damages to Food Lion Inc said deliberations took so long because one juror initially favored an award of $1.7 billion.

"We were at two extremes," one of the jurors, Tony Kinton, told Reuters after the jury returned its decision on Wednesday. "A couple of jurors felt it was a large amount that needed to be involved in the punitive damages, and there was one or two of us who felt like it should be a minimum amount, if any."

At one point during the six days of jury deliberations, an unnamed juror favored punishing ABC with punitive damages of $1.7 billion, Kinton said. After hours of discussions, a majority of the panel favored an award of about $8 million, he said.
"I thought a large amount was absurd and I stood my ground," Kinton said. "When we got it down to $8 million, I still refused."
Kinton said he proposed the $5.5 million figure as a compromise. "If I'm willing to go from zero to $5.5 million, certainly they should be willing to go from $8 million to $5.5 million," he said.
The federal jury of six men and six women voted to accept Kinton's proposal, he said.

The punitive damage award of $5.5 million came in Food Lion's lawsuit accusing ABC of fraud in a 1992 undercover report. The report, broadcast on "PrimeTime Live," showed Food Lion employees using unsafe and unsanitary practices in handling meat and other foods.

Jury foreman Greg Mack, speaking to reporters after the trial ended, said the panel wanted to punish ABC for approving an undercover report that had journalists falsifying job applications to Food Lion.
"I'm not expecting every news station in the world to shut down and not be able to operate. But you don't have to make up information, just leave off you're with ABC," Mack said.
Mack said jurors arrived at the $5.5 million figure for punitive damages based on the ABC journalists' job application.
"Misrepresentation on an application is not worth billions of dollars," Mack said. "Food Lion should take this as the message and not as the money."
Food Lion is a unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhalze Freres et Cie "LE LION" SA.
